main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snow roof slope above a log front wall with a plank door and two shuttered windows
top_band: Pale white-blue snow roof slope, rows ~8-34 (about 26 rows), with a thicker snow lip at rows 31-35 along the eave
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the light snow roof surface fills rows 8-34 and ends in a bright snow lip at the eave. Directly under it, rows 36-39 are a dark shadow with icicles. Below that is the log wall (rows 40-62) with an inset plank door, shuttered windows that have dark inner edges, and stacked log ends. This matches the Beodeul houses, where the roof reads as a foreshortened top slope above a vertical wall. No receding isometric side face is drawn.

style.flat_fills_note: The snow roof is smooth, but it carries blue shadow dabs and icicle detail.
style.evidence: The snow has about 4-5 steps (white, pale blue, mid blue-grey, shadow blue), and the wood has 4-5 browns. Outlines lean dark brown beside wood and dark navy beside the snow rather than neutral black. Texture comes from log grain, plank lines, icicles, the glowing windows, the stone chimney and scattered blue snow clumps. The large snow roof is smoother than the reference tile roofs, so density is slightly lower, but it holds up next to the references.
